habit_scope: habit South/Southwest (HUD RSDG §4.1). Fontana habit. Integral grade beam where frost is shallow (ORNL §1.3, Ch 4).
how_it_is_done: Site: compact; strip organics; termite prep including form stakes out of the pour; soil treatment before the slab; do not disturb treated soil (ORNL Ch 4; AF&PA Termites). Do not trade treatment for shields (D8).

Choose stem-wall + spread footing vs monolithic thickened edge (HUD §4.1; ORNL Figs 4-2, 4-3). D6 split: SOG thickened edge is the footing; do not apply the basement float rule as a veto on thickened-edge SOG (c-P05-D6-slab-bearing). Interior bearing: thicken the slab (HUD §4.6).
No subdrain and no waterproofing if the floor is above grade (ORNL Ch 4). High water table: raise the floor and put gravel under the slab.
Build-up: 2–3 in washed gravel or sand + 6-mil poly (HUD §4.6). Gravel is the capillary break. Slab 4 in min (ORNL note 16; HUD §4.6 ACI 302). Elevate slab ≥8 in above grade (ORNL Ch 4).
Isolation at the wall. Do not pour a basement-style shelf for the slab to sit on (ORNL Ch 4 citing ACI/BRAB) — that rule is for basement slabs; SOG thickened edge remains the footing (D6).

WWF or fibers if the slab is >10 ft in a direction (HUD §4.6); ORNL uses WWF for shrinkage/radon. Expansive soils: do not use the 4-in unreinforced habit; PTI/ACI 360 engineered path (HUD §4.6) — engineer, not a new Method from this set.

Edge insulation: exterior vertical foam is the only way to insulate a monolithic grade-beam edge; interior or under-slab foam must break the slab/wall thermal bridge (~R-5 in the joint) (ORNL §4.2). Fontana Title 24 2025 process hook lives here (mn-fontana) — energy, not a price.

Frost: habit is still bottom of footing below local frost (all three foundation sources). FPSF (foam in lieu of depth) is an engineered/IRC-prescriptive alternate that lets slabs into cold climates (HUD §4.8 ASCE 32-01; ORNL Ch 1/4). Not a separate unsourced method. Foam + termites: IRC/HUD restrict hidden paths unless the structure is termite-resistant.
Sill/anchors on stem or slab edge. This is the first floor in the South — no P07 joist package (c-P07-no-joists-on-sog; mn-fontana).
can_overlap_notes: Underslab MEP / radon / termite (P06) happens before the slab pour in the field. Phase spine still P05→P06→P07 as a stub; do not invent lag_days. Sequence hold: soil treatment before slab (ORNL).

tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources. Named: form stakes (out before pour); equipment bucket widths when a stem footing is used (HUD §4.4).

Footing / thickened-edge layout before pour; no frozen subgrade if any frost-depth stem is used.

No joist package on SOG South (c-P07-no-joists-on-sog).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit in the South/Southwest and Fontana. Beats basement when frost is shallow or when ORNL §1.3 water-table veto kills a basement. FPSF is the engineered/IRC path that lets a slab into cold climates without burying the footing — still this method, not a new type. Stem-wall vs monolithic is a D6 split inside this method.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Not the Wasatch/Logan 30-in-frost basement habit unless FPSF or frost-depth stem is designed. Expansive soils: 4-in unreinforced habit is a bad idea (HUD §4.6 PTI/ACI 360). Do not shop a P07 joist package on Fontana SOG.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: In the South and Inland Empire they did learn it — it is the habit. In basement markets they skip it unless frost is handled.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Foundation type (slab vs basement vs crawl) and any FPSF detail on drawings before permit. Engineer when expansive / tables fail.
risk_if_swapped_late: Slab vs basement after permit is a type change: no joists, no basement stairs, different excavation. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Down south and in Fontana the house sits on a slab: either a thickened edge that is the footing, or a short stem wall. Plastic under the slab, no drain tile if the floor is above the dirt. That slab is the first floor — do not order joists. Title 24 may want a thermal break at the edge; that is an insulation detail, not a new foundation type.
spanish_summary: En el Sur y en Fontana la casa va sobre losa: canto grueso que sirve de zapata, o una pared baja. Plástico debajo. Si el piso está arriba del terreno, no hay drenaje de cimiento. Esa losa es el primer piso — no pida viguetas. El código de energía puede pedir un corte térmico en el canto.
confidence_notes: SOG sequence and D6 split are sourced (high). Regional habit table med. FPSF as alt med. Title 24 2025 is orchestrator MarketNote hooked to ORNL §4.2, not a 2025 energy reprint.
open_gaps: Gap — book did not name a fail item
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring) not in these four books — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods.

fastener_schedule.pattern: through treated sill into wall (CIP/CMU, crawl wall, or slab stem/edge)
fastener_schedule.source: ORNL notes 13/31; AF&PA Sills. Embed D2 both variants (AF&PA ≥6 in CIP / ≥15 in block vs ORNL most codes ≥7 in / some 15 in masonry for uplift) — follow AHJ. Do not pick a winner.

labor_notes: Licensed applicator for termiticide is not named in the four books (termiticide itself is). Special inspector is not named. Crew counts: gap-crew-counts. Expansive soils: PTI/ACI 360 engineered path (HUD §4.6) — PE, not a new Method.

No subdrain/waterproofing if floor is above grade (ORNL Ch 4).
SOG thickened edge is the footing; basement float rule does not veto thickened-edge SOG (D6).
code_to_check: HUD prints IRC table R401.4.1 (presumptive soil bearing) and section R401.4 (when geotech reports are required). Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
HUD RSDG is an IRC companion. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. No R403/R404 in sources (gap-sop-irc-section-numbers).
FPSF: ASCE 32-01 (HUD §4.8). Engineered/IRC alt, not habit. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
ACI 302 slab 4 in min (HUD §4.6). Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
Expansive soils: PTI/ACI 360 (HUD §4.6). Confirm with engineer / AHJ.
time_money: No joist package on Fontana/South SOG. No drain tile/waterproof if the floor is above grade. Edge insulation/thermal break is a detailing add, not a new foundation type. No dollars in sources.
